STRATEGY: Parent is a mostly TFT-like strategy with retaliation and occasional defection; the trace simulates it against probes one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D; proposed changes are faster switching against always-defect, exploiting unconditional cooperators, better recovery from multiple defections, and endgame defection.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, maybe the simplest robust improvement over parent is to take parent and add:" and "We can design a strategy that uses conditional probabilities to decide whether to cooperate or defect."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-like strategy with forgiveness, occasional exploitation after long cooperation runs, and no endgame defection. The trace simulates the parent and candidate strategies against probe opponents (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and population slots. It proposes changes: defect on the last round, improve recovery from DD loops via forgiveness probes, and condition exploitation on the opponent's retaliation rate.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: "Parent's weakness against four_D_TFT: it takes long to recover. Parent code: if last_opp D and last_me D: if n>=4 and opp[-4:].count('D') >=3: return D; if rng.random()<0.35: return D; return C. So in DD, it defects if last 4 opp have >=3 D, else 35% D, 65% C. This means if opponent has been defecting a lot recently, it stays D. Against four_D_TFT, after initial 4 D, the opponent's last 4 are D. So parent will keep defecting! That's why recovery is poor. Because four_D_TFT defects 4 times, so opp[-4:].count('D') >=3 is true, so parent returns D. It never forgives until opponent's last 4 have fewer D's. But opponent is copying parent's D, so opponent keeps defecting. So parent is stuck in DD until it randomly cooperates? Wait, if parent always returns D, then opponent copies D, so opponent keeps D. So parent will never see fewer D's. The only way out is the rng.random()<0.35 check? But that check is inside the if last_opp=='D' and last_me=='D' block. The code: ... So if opp[-4:].count('D') >= 3, it ALWAYS returns D, never C. So against four_D_TFT, after 4 D's, opp[-4:] is all D, so parent always returns D. It gets stuck in DD forever!"
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "But the measured behavior says four_D_TFT: mutual_cooperation_last5=0.66, not_recovered=0.3, recovery_time=9.5. So it did recover sometimes. How?"
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness-and-exploitation strategy that cooperates early, retaliates after defections, and occasionally defects after long cooperation runs. The trace simulates it against always C, TFT, four_D_TFT, and periodic_D, and proposes changes: defect at n==99, add a 10% chance to cooperate even when the last four opponent moves contain ≥3 defections to break DD loops, and keep the existing exploitation rule.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's test this rule against one_D_TFT. one_D_TFT: opponent defects once at start. So opp_d = 1. So opp_d == 0 is false. So it won't trigger. Good."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates early, defects on long opponent-defection runs, and occasionally probes after cooperation streaks. The trace simulates endgame defection against never-defecting opponents and DD-loop recovery against TFT-like probes. It adds an n==99 defection and changes the long-DD branch to defect 90% / cooperate 10%.
